children: Sen.
Ted Cruz
(R-Texas) highlighted what he called strong economic data while arguing that gasoline prices remain below levels seen under former President Joe Biden.
On a recent episode of Verdict with Ted Cruz, Cruz and co-host
Ben Ferguson

discussed the Texas Senate race, Treasury developments involving Trump Accounts and school choice, and passengers who stopped a cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight to Israel. Cruz also discussed President Donald Trump’s message on the U.S. economy.
Cruz Highlights Income And Poverty Data
Cruz said the latest figures showed the U.S. had reached record levels for family income while poverty had fallen to its lowest recorded level.

"Median income is the highest it’s ever been recorded in the history of America," Cruz said. He added that the country also had "the lowest poverty rate that has ever been recorded in the history of America."
Cruz also pointed to what he described as the lowest recorded poverty rates among African-American, Hispanic and Native American populations.

He said Trump had been emphasizing those figures while responding to criticism over affordability. Cruz also addressed gasoline prices, saying they had increased but remained below levels during Biden’s presidency.
"But gas prices are still a lot lower than they were under Joe Biden," Cruz said.
